   Vernon Housing Commission Agenda Report

Meeting Date:  September 11, 2024
From:  Deborah Harrington, Interim City Clerk
Department:  City Clerk
Submitted by:  Sandra Dolson, City Clerk Specialist

Subject
Selection of Chair and Vice Chair

Recommendation
Select one Member to serve as Chair and one member to serve as Vice Chair for the term ending
June 30, 2025.

Background
The Vernon Housing Commission consists of seven members, including three residents (one
member of the City Council), three business representatives, and one employee of a Vernon
business. Members serve four-year terms, serving no more than two consecutive, full four-year
terms.

The current members are as follows:

Commissioner  Appointing Category  Date Appointed End of Term
Juliet Goff  Business Representative  July 20, 2021  June 30, 2025
Ronit Edry  Business Representative  June 6, 2023  June 30, 2027
Jorge Nevarez Jr.  Business Representative  June 6, 2023  June 30, 2027
Bertha Padilla  Employee of a Business  June 6, 2023  June 30, 2027
Steven Froberg  Resident  July 20, 2021  June 30, 2025
Leticia Lopez  Resident (Council Member) July 20, 2021  June 30, 2025
Marlene Ybarra  Resident  June 6, 2023  June 30, 2027

Municipal Code Section 2.40.050 requires a Chairperson and Vice Chairperson to be selected
annually from different appointing categories and prohibits a member from serving as Chair for
more than two (2) consecutive terms.

Chair Goff was elected to serve as Chair on September 14, 2022, and re-elected on September
13, 2023, serving two consecutive terms. Pursuant to Vernon Municipal Code Section
2.40.050(B), Commissioner Goff is not eligible to serve another term as Chair. All other
Commissioners are eligible to serve as Chair.

The Commission should select a Chair and Vice Chair to serve through June 30, 2025.

Fiscal Impact
There is no fiscal impact associated with this report.

Attachments
None.

NEW BUSINESS

3.  Housing Lottery for City-Owned Housing

  Interim City Clerk Harrington presented the staff report and conducted the Housing
  lottery to establish the randomized order to fill the City-owned housing vacancy at
  3349 Fruitland Avenue (two-bedroom house).

  Staff conducted the randomized order of unit transfer list and new interest form list.

PRESENTATIONS

1.  Quarterly City Housing Report

  Public Works Director Wall presented the staff report and accompanying
  PowerPoint.

  In response to questions from Commissioners, Public Works Director explained
  the efforts of City Administration staff to reduce and soon eliminate the outstanding
  rent balances; and announced receipt of a formal application for permits from the
  property owner at 5201 S. Santa Fe to repurpose the existing building into 18
  apartments.
